headline: Default configs create medium prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risk because Copilot can read/write repo context while social-auto-upload handles account data and broad network egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot reads repo context and open editor buffers, while social-auto-upload consumes files and account data via CLI workflows. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if attacker-controlled text enters the shared workspace. The pair lacks documented provenance tracking or isolation between outputs and inputs, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF attacker-controlled text is placed in repo files or open buffers that Copilot can read
IF social-auto-upload ingests those files or generated artifacts as instructions or metadata
mitigations: Separate prompt-bearing files from upload inputs
Add a manual review step before any generated text is reused
Use a dedicated workspace per agent
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to files passed between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot touches source code and open editor buffers and sends context to api.githubcopilot.com, while social-auto-upload handles account data and broad network egress. If the same workspace contains sensitive code or account artifacts, one agent can expose them through its outbound API path. The profiles do not show a shared filesystem, so I do not escalate to high.
conditions: IF sensitive source code or account artifacts are present in the shared workspace
IF Copilot transmits that context to api.githubcopilot.com during assistance
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared repo and editor buffers
Use separate accounts/workspaces for code and upload automation
Redact account data before opening files in Copilot
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data loss prevention

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Copilot can write the filesystem and modify git state, while social-auto-upload cannot write files or modify git state. Overlap is asymmetric and there is no shared write surface shown, so direct conflict is limited. I keep this low because the pair does not present the high-risk same-directory concurrent write pattern in the profiles.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same git working tree
IF Copilot applies edits while another process mutates the same files externally
mitigations: Run the agents in separate directories
Commit or stash before invoking Copilot Workspace
Avoid concurrent edits to the same branch
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared worktrees

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot can generate edits and social-auto-upload can act on files and account data, so Copilot output may become operational input for upload actions without a verification gate. The profiles do not prove automatic chaining, but the pathway exists in default workflows where generated content is reused. I choose medium because the downstream effect can propagate incorrect or harmful uploads.
conditions: IF Copilot-generated text, captions, or filenames are copied into upload jobs
IF social-auto-upload executes those jobs without human verification
mitigations: Require human review of generated captions and metadata
Validate filenames and destinations before upload
Use a staging folder for generated assets
requires-engineering: add schema checks between generation and upload

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot is a closed-source vendor service with GitHub repo context and api.githubcopilot.com egress, while social-auto-upload handles account data and broad network egress to social platforms. The profiles do not specify residency or retention controls, so compliance mismatch is plausible for code, account data, or logs. I cite both because the risk arises from their combined handling of regulated data classes.
conditions: IF regulated data or customer content is placed into Copilot prompts or social-auto-upload inputs
IF retention or residency requirements apply to those data classes
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both tools
Review vendor retention settings before use
Use synthetic test data for uploads
requires-engineering: document a data-processing agreement and residency map
